bank.q: Consider the following statements about the shrinking divisible pool:
s: Cesses and surcharges are excluded from the pool shared with states.
The 16th Finance Commission recommended CAG-certified disclosure of net proceeds.
Its grand bargain proposal would raise the states' percentage share while keeping the pool unchanged.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The grand bargain works the other way — a smaller percentage share of a materially larger pool.

bank.q: Match List I (institution) with List II (constitutional or statutory basis):
bank.e: The Finance Commission and GST Council are constitutional bodies, the Inter-State Council sits in Article 263, and NITI Aayog rests on nothing more than a Cabinet resolution.

bank.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: The River Boards Act, 1956 has never been effectively used
GST Council recommendations are persuasive rather than binding
The Sixth Schedule currently extends to Ladakh
Residuary powers vest in Parliament under Article 248
bank.e: Extending the Sixth Schedule to Ladakh is a demand, not a fact. It presently applies to tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

bank.as: Local bodies remain the weakest tier of Indian federalism despite two constitutional amendments.
bank.rs: Fewer than a fifth of states have fully devolved the Eleventh Schedule subjects, and municipal revenues stand at about 1% of GDP.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — functions without finances and functionaries, in the standard formulation.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about routes for Parliament to legislate on State subjects:
s: Article 249 requires a Rajya Sabha resolution passed by special majority.
Article 252 requires resolutions from two or more state legislatures.
Article 253 requires the prior consent of the states concerned.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Article 253, the treaty-implementation route, needs no state consent at all — which is why it is the widest of the three.

bank.q: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a doctrine with its function?
o: Pith and substance — resolving conflict between two Union laws
Colourable legislation — testing legislative competence, not motive
Territorial nexus — determining which Finance Commission formula applies
bank.e: Colourable legislation asks only whether the legislature had the power, per K. C. Gajapati Deo. Bona fides are irrelevant.

bank.q: All of the following are unitary features of the Indian Constitution EXCEPT:
o: Parliament's power to alter state boundaries under Article 3
The Comptroller and Auditor General auditing state accounts
States' power to tax major minerals recognised in 2024
bank.e: That 2024 development expands state fiscal space, running against the unitary grain rather than reinforcing it.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
items: The 73rd and 74th Amendments come into force
bank.e: The 73rd and 74th Amendments came into force in 1993 → S. R. Bommai in 1994 → NITI Aayog in 2015 → GST in 2017. The trap is that the Amendments were passed in 1992 but commenced in 1993, still ahead of Bommai.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the Governor:
s: The office holds during the pleasure of the President.
B. P. Singhal held that removal cannot be arbitrary.
The Supreme Court's 2025 assent timelines remain in force.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The April 2025 timelines were reversed later that year while the Court answered a Presidential Reference.

bank.as: Water disputes persist even between states governed by the same party.
bank.rs: Water allocation tracks river basins and regional identity rather than party lines.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the Mahanadi dispute, pending since 2018, is the standing illustration.
